title.analysis: Authentic title "If I Started Investing in August 2026, This is What I'd Buy" is a dated, first-person allocation promise. The script delivers market context, an account order of operations, a three-fund portfolio with tickers, fee and behaviour evidence. TYPICAL (0.77x) against a very young cohort (14-24 days) with low absolute views; two STRONG peers. Association only; no CTR or experiment evidence.

script.opening_words: You've got money sitting in checking doing nothing, and this year you've opened your brokerage app maybe 40 times without buying a single thing. Same loop every time. The market's at an all-time high, which feels like the worst possible moment to buy. So, you close the app. 3 weeks later, it's at a new all-time high, which somehow feels worse. Here's the part that should bother you. The boring, federally insured, nothing can go wrong cash sitting in your
script.ending_words: Three funds, 4/100 of a percent, and the deeply unglamorous discipline of staying boring on purpose for longer than feels reasonable to you. Welcome to the least impressive strategy that works. The market doesn't pay you for being clever, it pays you for being present. So, the only real question left isn't what you should buy in August of 2026, it's whether you'll still own it in August of 2056.
script.analysis: Full 20307 canonical characters read. A dated allocation guide: frozen-buyer hook and cash-vs-stocks expected return, market context (S&P level, CAPE vs forward P/E, concentration), order of operations (match, HSA, Roth, 401(k), taxable), one-fund VT answer, three-fund 60/20/20 with tickers, fund-fee drag (Fidelity Freedom vs Freedom Index), international case (2000s, Nikkei), bonds and I bonds, optional sleeves (small-cap value, dividends, gold, Bitcoin), behaviour gap (Morningstar, holding periods, J.P. Morgan best days, SPIVA), 2007 and 2020 recoveries, Fidelity "dead accounts" folklore (correctly flagged as unverified), averages vs medians and close. Verified: S&P ~7,700-7,800, 30-year Treasury 5.31% 19-year high, CPI 3.4%, 2026 IRA/401(k) limits, best-days pattern. Reproduces: blended fee, $566K fee example (annual convention), return gap share. Problems: "VT or VOO" for the US slice; 51% saving at target conflated with missing the match; best-days period label; thumbnail implies a 2026-2030 forecast. The stored ending is complete.

Bonds, Treasuries and I bonds; long-bond caveat.
Sleeves: small-cap value, dividends, gold, Bitcoin.
Behaviour gap, holding periods, best days, SPIVA.
Cost of paralysis; averages vs medians.
Close: Trisha's plan, Reggie and Delia, own it in 2056.
